children.text: Computer Networks: Week-12 Assignment

A MAC address is typically how many bits long?
A.
B.
C.
D.
16 bits 32 bits 48 bits 64 bits
Ans: C (48 bits)

Traffic between different VLANs requires the use of a:
A.
B.
C.
D.

Bridge
Hub
Repeater
Layer 3 device
Ans: D (Layer 3 device)

What does an ARP cache store?
A.
B.
C.
D.

Port numbers and socket information
IP address and MAC address pairs
Domain names and IP addresses
Routes to different networks
Ans: B (IP address and MAC address pairs)

The main function of a MAC address is to:
A.
B.
C.
D.

Identify websites
Route packets across the Internet
Deliver frames within the same LAN
Assign IP addresses
Ans: C (Deliver frames within the same LAN)

How is an ARP request sent to all hosts on a LAN?
A.
B.
C.
D.

As a unicast message to the router
As a broadcast message
As a multicast message to a specific group
As a unicast message to all hosts sequentially
Ans: B (As a broadcast message)

Which protocol maps an IP address to a MAC address?
A.
B.
C.
D.

DHCP
DNS
ARP
ICMP
Ans: C (ARP)

A network administrator creates VLAN 10 for the Computer Science Department and VLAN
20 for the Electrical Department on the same switch. PC X belongs to VLAN 10, and PC Y
belongs to VLAN 20. PC X sends an ARP broadcast. What happens to the ARP broadcast?
A.
B.
C.
D.

It is received by all devices in both VLAN 10 and VLAN 20
It is received only by devices in VLAN 10
It is received only by PC Y in VLAN 20
It is discarded by the switch
Ans: B (It is received only by devices in VLAN 10)

Which transmission mode allows simultaneous communication in both directions?
A.
B.
C.
D.

Simplex
Half duplex
Full duplex
Broadcast
Ans: C (Full duplex)

What is the technique used to convert binary data into digital signals for transmission?
A.
B.
C.
D.

Modulation
Encryption
Demodulation
Line coding
Ans: D (Line coding)

10. Which technology became the dominant LAN technology?
       A.   Ethernet
       B.   Token Ring
       C.   ATM
       D.   FDDI
Ans: A (Ethernet)
Computer Networks: Week-11 Assignment

Which of the following is NOT a primary service provided by the Link Layer?
A.
B.
C.
D.

Framing
Error detection
Reliable delivery over a link
End-to-end process communication
Ans: D (End-to-end process communication)

In CSMA, what does a station do before transmitting?
A.
B.
C.
D.

Listens to the channel to check if another device is transmitting
Sends a request to the receiver
Waits for a token to arrive
Divides the channel into frequency bands
Ans: A (Listens to the channel to check if another device is transmitting)

A collision occurs when:
A.
B.
C.
D.

A frame reaches its destination
A router drops a packet
A switch receives duplicate MAC addresses
Two or more stations transmit simultaneously on a shared medium
Ans: D (Two or more stations transmit simultaneously on a shared medium)

In RTS/CTS communication, which message is sent first?
A.
B.
C.
D.

CTS
RTS
ACK
DATA
Ans: B (RTS)
bits
so
that
some
errors
can
be corrected without

Which  technique  adds  redundant
retransmission?
A.   ARQ
B.   CRC
C.   Forward Error Correction
D.   Backward Error Correction
Ans: C (Forward Error Correction)

Which error detection technique is especially effective at detecting burst errors?
A.
B.
C.
D.

Simple parity
Two-dimensional parity
Checksum
Cyclic Redundancy Check
Ans: D (Cyclic Redundancy Check)

What is the function of the jam signal in CSMA/CD?
A.
B.
C.
D.

To start transmission
To indicate a successful transmission
To inform all stations about a collision
To request retransmission from the sender
Ans: C (To inform all stations about a collision)

What is two-dimensional parity checking used for?
A.
B.
C.
D.

Flow control
Forward error correction
Link access control
Framing
Ans: B (Forward error correction)

Why is error detection performed at every hop in the Link Layer?
A.
B.
C.
D.

To replace transport-layer reliability
To reduce packet size
To reduce routing complexity
To discard corrupted frames early and avoid wasting network resources
Ans: D (To discard corrupted frames early and avoid wasting network resources)

10. Wireless networks require stronger error detection because they are more affected by:
       A.   Encryption
       B.   Routing loops
       C.   Interference
       D.   IP fragmentation
Ans: C (Interference)
Computer Networks: Week-10 Assignment

What port does BGP use to establish TCP sessions between routers?
A.
B.
C.
D.
Ans: C (179)

What information does BGP advertise?
A.
B.
C.
D.

MAC addresses
IP prefixes and path information
DNS records
VLAN IDs
Ans: B (IP prefixes and path information)

Which ICMPv6 protocol replaces ARP in IPv6 networks?
A.
B.
C.
D.

IGMP
DHCPv6
DNS
NDP
Ans: D (NDP)

Which BGP message is exchanged first after a TCP connection is established?
A.
B.
C.
D.

UPDATE
KEEPALIVE
OPEN
ECHO
Ans: C (OPEN)

Which BGP message is used to maintain an established session?
A.
B.
C.
D.

OPEN
UPDATE
RESET
KEEPALIVE
Ans: D (KEEPALIVE)

Hot Potato Routing selects the:
A.
B.
C.
D.

Closest NEXT-HOP router
Longest AS-PATH
Highest bandwidth link
Lowest router ID
Ans: A (Closest NEXT-HOP router)

ICMP messages are encapsulated inside:
A.
B.
C.
D.

TCP segments
IP packets
UDP datagrams
Ethernet frames only
Ans: B (IP packets)

Which network utility uses ICMP Echo Request and Echo Reply messages?
A.
B.
C.
D.

FTP
Telnet
SMTP
Ping
Ans: D (Ping)

Which ICMP message informs a host about a better route to a destination?
A.
B.
C.
D.

Destination Unreachable
Time Exceeded
Redirect
Parameter Problem
Ans: C (Redirect)

10. Which ICMP message is generated when a packet's TTL expires?
       A.   Destination Unreachable
       B.   Time Exceeded
       C.   Redirect
       D.   Echo Reply
Ans: B (Time Exceeded)
Computer Networks: Week-9 Assignment

Which routing algorithm requires every router to have complete knowledge of the network
topology?
A.
B.
C.
D.

Distance vector
Link state
RIP
DHCP
Ans: B (Link state)

In Poisoned Reverse, if y is the next hop for z to reach destination x, what does z advertise to
y?
A.
B.
C.
D.

The normal distance to x
A reduced metric to x
That its distance to x is infinity
A better alternative path
Ans: C (That its distance to x is infinity)

Which loop prevention technique prevents advertising a route back to the router from which
it was learned?
A.
B.
C.
D.

Route poisoning
Dijkstra algorithm
HELLO protocol
Split horizon
Ans: D (Split horizon)

The Count-to-Infinity problem is associated with:
A.
B.
C.
D.

OSPF
DHCP
Distance Vector Routing
IS-IS
Ans: C (Distance Vector Routing)

How often does RIP send routing updates by default?
A.
B.
C.
D.
Every 15 seconds Every 30 seconds Every 60 seconds Every 90 seconds
Ans: B (Every 30 seconds)

In Distance Vector routing, what is the meaning of "Triggered Update"?
A.
B.
C.
D.

Propagating link failure information immediately
Sending updates exactly every 30 seconds
Updating the routing table every 15 hops
Sending HELLO messages continuously
Ans: A (Propagating link failure information immediately)

What happens when HELLO messages stop arriving in OSPF?
A.
B.
C.
D.

The router continues normal operation
The neighbor is considered down and routes are recalculated
The router initiates a DHCP request
The router increases its hop count
Ans: B (The neighbor is considered down and routes are recalculated)

RIP uses which transport protocol and port number?
A.
B.
C.
D.

TCP 80
TCP 179
UDP 520
UDP 53
Ans: C (UDP 520)

What is the maximum valid hop count allowed in RIP?
A.
B.
C.
D.
Ans: B (15)

10. Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Link State routing?
       A.   Routers share entire routing tables with neighbors
       B.   Routers calculate shortest path using Dijkstra
       C.   Routers maintain a synchronized view of network topology
       D.   Routers exchange link-state databases
Ans: A (Routers share entire routing tables with neighbors)
Computer Networks: Week-8 Assignment

Which of the following is the primary function of forwarding in the network layer?
A.
B.
C.
D.

Selecting the shortest path between networks
Assigning IP addresses to hosts
Detecting transmission errors
Moving packets from an input link to the appropriate output link
Ans: D (Moving packets from an input link to the appropriate output link)

If a router's output buffer is full and a new packet arrives, which drop policy is typically
applied, where the newest packet is dropped?
A.
B.
C.
D.

Random Early Detection
Tail Drop
Priority Drop
Head Drop
Ans: (B) Tail Drop
A router's forwarding table contains the following entries:
A packet destined for 192.168.10.144 arrives. Which entry will be used for forwarding?

A.
B.
C.
D.

If the switching fabric is slower than the combined input port rates, what may occur?
A.
B.
C.
D.

Packet duplication
Queueing at input ports
Packet encryption
Routing loops
Ans: B (Queueing at input ports)
Prefix
Interface
Interface A
Interface B
Interface C

children.text:
Which scheduling algorithm allocates bandwidth fairly while assigning different weights to
different traffic classes?
A.
B.
C.
D.

Tail drop
Round robin
Priority scheduling
Weighted fair queueing
Ans: D (Weighted fair queueing)

In the input port of a router, what functions are typically performed?
A.
B.
C.
D.

Packet scheduling and output queueing
Routing algorithm calculation and forwarding table updates
Line termination, decapsulation, and forwarding table lookup
Segmentation and reassembly of data
Ans: C (Line termination, decapsulation, and forwarding table lookup)

Output buffering is required when:
A.
B.
C.
D.

Output link speed is greater than arrival rate
Routers have empty queues
Routing tables become full
Arrival rate exceeds output link transmission speed
Ans: D (Arrival rate exceeds output link transmission speed)

Why is Longest Prefix Matching used in IP routing?
A.
B.
C.
D.

It always selects the route with the fewest network hops
It is required by the TCP protocol to establish a connection
It allows routers to forward packets using only the destination MAC address
It is necessary because of the hierarchical and classless nature of IP addressing to select
the most specific matching route
Ans: D (It is necessary because of the hierarchical and classless nature of IP addressing to select the most specific matching route)

What is the primary function of a Ternary Content Addressable Memory (TCAM) in a modern
router?
A.
B.
C.
D.

To store routing tables and perform Longest Prefix Matching in a single clock cycle
To perform routing calculations for the control plane
To buffer packets that are experiencing output port contention
To convert IP addresses from decimal to binary format
Ans: A (To store routing tables and perform Longest Prefix Matching in a single clock cycle)
10. A router's forwarding table is:
For a packet destined to IP address 10.1.2.99, which port will the router use?

A.
B.
C.
D.
Port 1 Port 2 Port 3 Port 4
Ans: C (Port 3)
Prefix
Output Port
Port 1
Port 2
Port 3
Port 4

children.text: Computer Networks: Week-7 Assignment

Why does TCP use sequence numbers?
       A.
       B.
       C.
       D.

To encrypt transmitted data
To identify applications
To enable reliable and ordered delivery of data
To determine the IP address of the receiver
Ans: (C) To enable reliable and ordered delivery of data

A TCP Reno sender is in the congestion avoidance phase with a congestion window (cwnd) of 24 MSS and a slow-start threshold (ssthresh) of 16 MSS. It receives three duplicate ACKs. What will be the new values of cwnd and ssthresh immediately after this event?
A.
B.
C.
D.
cwnd = 24 MSS, ssthresh = 12 MSS cwnd = 12 MSS, ssthresh = 12 MSS cwnd = 15 MSS, ssthresh = 12 MSS cwnd = 1 MSS, ssthresh = 12 MSS
Ans: (C) cwnd = 15 MSS, ssthresh = 12 MSS

A TCP receiver advertises a receive window of 8000 bytes. The sender has transmitted bytes up to sequence number 9500 and has received an ACK up to sequence number 2000. How many additional bytes can the sender transmit immediately without violating the receiver's flow control limit?
A. 500 bytes
B. 1500 bytes
C. 6000 bytes
D. 7500 bytes
Ans: A (500 bytes)

A TCP Tahoe connection is in the congestion avoidance phase with a congestion window (cwnd) of 20 MSS and a slow-start threshold (ssthresh) of 16 MSS. A retransmission timeout (RTO) occurs. What will be the new values of cwnd and ssthresh, and which phase will the connection enter next?
A.
B.
C.
D.

cwnd = 1 MSS, ssthresh = 10 MSS, enters Slow Start
cwnd = 10 MSS, ssthresh = 10 MSS, enters Congestion Avoidance
cwnd = 13 MSS, ssthresh = 16 MSS, enters Fast Recovery
cwnd = 20 MSS, ssthresh = 16 MSS, remains in Congestion Avoidance
Ans: (A) cwnd = 1 MSS, ssthresh = 10 MSS, enters Slow Start

A TCP receiver has a receive buffer size of 10,000 bytes. The last byte received is
8,500, and the last byte read by the receiving application is 3,500. What advertised
window (rwnd) value should the receiver send?
A.
B.
C.
D.
1500 bytes 3500 bytes 5000 bytes 8500 bytes
Ans: (C) 5000 bytes

Assume that the TCP sender's window size permits the transmission of four TCP
segments. Which statement is correct?
A.
B.

C.
D.

The sender must receive an ACK after every segment before transmitting the
next segment
The   sender   can   transmit   up   to   four   TCP   segments   before   waiting   for
acknowledgments
The sender can transmit only one TCP segment at a time
The sender retransmits every segment immediately after transmission

Ans: (b) The sender can transmit up to four TCP segments before waiting for
acknowledgments

A TCP connection has a congestion window (cwnd) of 12,000 bytes and a receiver
advertised window (rwnd) of 8,000 bytes. The sender has transmitted data up to
byte 15,000 and has received ACKs up to byte 9,000. How much more data can the
sender transmit?
A.
B.
C.
D.
2000 bytes 3000 bytes 4000 bytes 6000 bytes
Ans: (A) 2000 bytes

What is the primary purpose of TCP flow control?
A.
B.
C.
D.

Prevent packet corruption during transmission
Prevent the sender from overwhelming the receiver
Prevent congestion in the network routers
Prevent unauthorized access to transmitted data
Ans: (B) Prevent the sender from overwhelming the receiver

A TCP connection begins in the Slow Start phase with an initial congestion window
(cwnd) of 1 MSS. Assuming no packet loss occurs, what will be the value of cwnd
after 4 RTTs?
A.   4 MSS

B.
C.
D.

8 MSS
16 MSS 32 MSS
Ans: C (16 MSS)
the
sender
typically
detects

10. In   an   implicit  congestion  notification  mechanism,
       network congestion based on:
       A.   Router generated congestion messages
       B.   The ECE flag set in the TCP header
       C.   The receiver's advertised window (rwnd)
       D.   Packet loss or increased round-trip delay
Ans: (D) Packet loss or increased round-trip delay
Computer Networks: Week-6 Assignment

Which of the following is not a type of error or issue encountered during network data
transmission?
      A.
      B.
      C.
      D.

Bit errors
Burst errors
Packet drops
Arithmetic overflow
Ans: (D) Arithmetic overflow
the
receiver
receives

A   sender   transmits   the   following   bit   sequence   11010110   and
11011110. What type of error has occurred during transmission?
       A.   Bit error
       B.   Byte error
       C.   Burst error
       D.   No error
Ans: (A) Bit error

A sender transmits the packets in the following order P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6 and the receiver
receives the packets as P1, P3, P2, P5, P6.   Which of the following correctly identifies the
transmission issues?
       A.   Only packet loss has occurred
       B.   Only out-of-order delivery has occurred
       C.   Packet loss and out-of-order delivery have occurred
       D.   Duplicate packets and packet loss have occurred
Ans: (C) Packet loss and out-of-order delivery have occurred

Which of the following is an assumption made by the rdt 2.0 (Reliable Data Transfer 2.0)
protocol?
       A.
       B.
       C.
       D.

Packets may be lost during transmission
The channel may introduce bit errors, but packets are never lost
Both packet loss and corruption may occur
ACK/NAK messages may get corrupted or lost
Ans: (B) The channel may introduce bit errors, but packets are never lost

Which of the following correctly describes the difference between ACK and NACK in reliable
data transfer protocols?
A. ACK indicates packet corruption, while NACK indicates successful reception
B. ACK indicates successful reception of a packet, while NACK indicates that a packet
was not received correctly or is corrupted
C. Both ACK and NACK indicate successful reception, but with different priorities
D. ACK and NACK are used only for detecting packet loss, not errors
Ans: (B) ACK indicates successful reception of a packet, while NACK indicates that a packet
was not received correctly or is corrupted

rdt 3.0 is designed to operate over unreliable channels that may introduce bit errors and
packet loss. However, duplicate packets may still be received due to retransmissions. How
does rdt 3.0 handle such duplicate packets?
       A.
       B.
       C.
       D.

It ignores packet loss but delivers duplicates to the application layer
It prevents duplicates by ensuring packets are never retransmitted
It uses sequence numbers to detect and discard duplicate packets at the receiver
It relies on ACK only and does not use any mechanism for duplicates
Ans: (C) It uses sequence numbers to detect and discard duplicate packets at the receiver

What is the primary mechanism used in rdt 3.0 to detect packet loss during transmission?
A. Timer
B. Sequence numbers
C. ACK/NAK mismatch
D. Packet reordering
Ans: (A) Timer
A video streaming server is sending data to a client over a high-speed network. The link has a
bandwidth of 120 Mbps, and the round-trip time (RTT) between the server and client is 80
ms. What is the Delay Bandwidth Product (DBP) for this network link?
A. 9.6 Mb
B. 12 Mb
C. 960 Mb
D. 0.96 Mb
Ans: (A) 9.6 Mb

In the Go-Back N protocol the receiver on receipt of out-of-order packet does the following
       A.
       B.
       C.
       D.

Can discard the packet
Re-ACK pkt with highest in-order seq #
send a NACK
Send nothing
Ans: (A) Can discard the packet and (B) Re-ACK pkt with highest in-order seq #

10. A sender uses Selective Repeat ARQ with a window size of 4 and sequence numbers from 0
       to 7. The sender transmits packets 0, 1, 2, 3. If packet 1 is lost, while packets 0, 2, and 3 are
       received correctly and buffered at the receiver. Assume individual ACKs are used, and only
       the lost packet is retransmitted. How many total transmissions are required to correctly
       deliver all packets?
              A.   4
              B.   5
              C.   6
              D.   7
Ans: (B) 5
Computer Networks: Week-5 Assignment

Which of the following are not essential services offered by a transport layer protocol
       A.
       B.
       C.
       D.

Multiplexing
Segmentation
Error detection
Error correction
Ans: (C) Error detection and (D) Error correction

Following is the name assigned to the data unit at the transport layer
       A.
       B.
       C.
       D.

Packet
Chunk
Segment
Frame
Ans: (C) Segment

Multiplexing and demultiplexing with TCP connection happens with
       A.
       B.
       C.
       D.

Source and Destination port numbers
Source and Destination port numbers and Source and Destination IP addresses
Source and Destination IP addresses
Source IP address and Destination port number
Ans: (B) Source and Destination port numbers and Source and Destination IP addresses

Which statement best describes multiplexing and demultiplexing in the User Datagram Protocol (UDP)?
A. Multiplexing combines data from multiple applications into UDP segments using
       source port numbers, while demultiplexing delivers received segments to the correct
       application using the destination port number.
B. Multiplexing encrypts UDP data before transmission, while demultiplexing decrypts
       it at the receiver.
C. Multiplexing guarantees reliable delivery of UDP packets, while demultiplexing
       detects and retransmits lost packets.
D. Multiplexing fragments large UDP packets, while demultiplexing reassembles them
       at the destination.

Ans: (A) Multiplexing combines data from multiple applications into UDP segments using source port numbers, while demultiplexing delivers received segments to the correct application using the destination port number.

Which of the following are true w.r.t UDP
       A.
       B.
       C.
       D.

It incurs one RTT time for connection establishment
It does not incur any RTT for connection establishment
It has smaller header size compared to TCP
It does not provide error detection capabilities
Ans: (B) It does not incur any RTT for connection establishment and (C) It has smaller header size compared to TCP

Which of the following application layer protocols use UDP
       A.
       B.
       C.
       D.

DNS
SNMP
HTTP
ARP
Ans: (A) DNS and (B) SNMP

Which of the following fields are included in the UDP pseudo header during UDP checksum
calculation?
A. Source IP Address, Destination IP Address, Protocol Number, UDP Length
B. Source MAC Address, Destination MAC Address, Protocol Number, UDP Checksum
C. Source IP Address, Destination IP Address, Source Port, Destination Port
D. Source MAC Address, Destination MAC Address, Source Port, Destination Port
